sentences: What if you invested your baby's Child Benefit instead of spending it?
By their eighteenth birthday, it could be worth about {£46,000.|forty six thousand pounds.}
For your first child, Child Benefit is {£27.05|twenty seven pounds and five pence} a week.
It's paid until they turn {16,|sixteen,} or longer if they stay in education.
That's {£1,406|one thousand four hundred and six pounds} a year, or about {£117|one hundred and seventeen pounds} a month.
Over sixteen years, that adds up to about {£22,500.|twenty two thousand five hundred pounds.}
Now invest it in a Junior Stocks {&|and} Shares ISA instead.
At {7%|seven per cent} a year, it could grow to about {£40,000|forty thousand} by age {16.|sixteen.}
The money is locked until {18,|eighteen,} so it keeps growing, to about {£46,000.|forty six thousand.}
Leave it until they're thirty? Over {£100,000.|a hundred thousand pounds.}
Earn over {£80,000?|eighty thousand?} You'd pay it all back in tax, but you should still claim, and opt out of the payments.
That way you still get National Insurance credits towards your State Pension while your child is under {12.|twelve.}
And the Junior ISA limit is {£9,000|nine thousand pounds} a year, so grandparents can pay in too.
Your turn. With two children, roughly how much could Child Benefit grow to by eighteen? Comment your guess.
This is an illustration. Investments can fall, and you may get back less.
